## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sīlavīmaṁsakajātaka* (Ja 86), translated as *A Test of Virtue*, belongs to the Pali Jātaka collection. According to the traditional narrative framework, the Buddha related this story while residing at Jetavana about a brahmin who put his reputation for goodness to the test. A closely related version of the introductory narrative appears in Jātaka 362, in which a protagonist resolves the question of whether moral conduct or erudition is superior, concluding that virtue (*sīla*) is indeed higher than learning (*suta*) [Readings from the Jatakas].
